teach_overlay.label: Cancer genes are our own genes
teach_overlay.who_card: Peter K. Vogt (born 1932) — German-American virologist and geneticist · Robert A. Weinberg (born 1942) — American cancer biologist
teach_overlay.timeline_step: 3/4 · 11 Mar 1976 (Stehelin, Varmus, Bishop & Vogt prove viral src is a captured normal cellular proto-oncogene c-src; 1989 Nobel Prize)

plates.side_label: 11 MAR 1976 STEHELIN, VARMUS, BISHOP & VOGT (NATURE 260: 170–173): VIRAL V-SRC IS STOLEN CELLULAR PROTO-ONCOGENE C-SRC + 1982 HUMAN HRAS CODON 12 G→T TYPO

plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked Stehelin, Varmus, Bishop & Vogt (11 March 1976, Nature 260: 170–173) radioactive cDNA hybridization curve shows viral v-src probe binding strongly to uninfected normal chicken, duck, quail, turkey, and emu cellular DNA (proving c-src is a conserved vertebrate proto-oncogene, plus Weinberg/Barbacid 1982 single G->T codon 12 mutation in human HRAS).

teach_overlay.label: 11 MAR 1976 BISHOP & VARMUS (NATURE): VIRAL SRC HYBRIDIZES TO NORMAL CELLULAR C-SRC PROTO-ONCOGENE + 1982 HUMAN HRAS G→T TYPO
teach_overlay.detail: Inked Stehelin, Varmus, Bishop & Vogt (11 March 1976, Nature 260: 170–173) radioactive cDNA hybridization curve on period paper showing viral v-src probe binding strongly to uninfected normal chicken, duck, quail, turkey, and emu cellular DNA (proving c-src is a conserved vertebrate proto-oncogene, plus Weinberg/Barbacid 1982 single G->T codon 12 mutation in human HRAS)
teach_overlay.scale: Peyton Rous's virus didn't bring an alien poison into the cell — like a car thief who hot-wires your own ignition, it stole a normal growth gene that every healthy cell uses to heal wounds and welded the gas pedal to the floor
